Split the conjunction, and for the equivalence prove both universally quantified statements independently.

For the first claim, use the open cover \((U_i)\) to localize on \(f^{-1}(U_i)\). Continuity of \(iV_i\) makes \(iV_i^{-1}(O)\) open for every open \(O\subseteq X\). Since \(f\circ iV_i\) is an embedding, this open set is the inverse image of some open \(W_i\subseteq Y\). The covering condition \(f^{-1}(U_i)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(iV_i)\) then gives
\[
O=f^{-1}\!\left(\bigcup_i(U_i\cap W_i)\right),
\]
showing that \(f\) is inducing. Injectivity follows similarly: choose a chart over an \(U_i\) containing the common value of two points and use injectivity of \(f\circ iV_i\).

For the left side of the `Iff`, the map
\[
x\longmapsto (U\mapsto x\in U)
\]
represents the topology of \(X\) by Sierpiński-valued characteristic functions. Each coordinate is continuous, and every open \(U\) is recovered as the inverse image of the open truth-value under the \(U\)-coordinate, proving inducingness.

For the right side, view matrices as finite products of the coefficient ring. An embedding \(R\to S\) induces an embedding on matrices entrywise. The special linear groups carry the corresponding subtype topologies, and determinant compatibility gives
\[
A\in \mathrm{SL}_n(R)\iff \operatorname{map}(A)\in \mathrm{SL}_n(S);
\]
the reverse implication uses injectivity of the ring embedding. Thus the matrix embedding restricts to an embedding of special linear groups. Since both sides of the `Iff` hold outright, assemble the equivalence without deriving either statement from the other.
